scope.rule: These proficiencies are added to the class lists of the anti-paladin, barbarian, dwarven machinist, and dwarven delver.

rules.rule: The character may fight wearing armor up to 2 points heavier than normally permitted by class without penalty.
Does not grant the ability to cast spells in armor.
Does not grant the ability to use thief skills in armor heavier than leather.
Does not allow benefit from proficiencies or class powers that forbid use of certain armor.
The character may design automatons as if two class levels higher than actual level.
Time required to design automatons is reduced by 20%.
The character may repair automatons as if two class levels higher than actual level.
The character may perform hasty repairs in 10 minutes (1 turn) instead of 1 hour.
Hasty repairs last 4d6 turns.
Any hp repaired by hasty repairs are lost when the duration ends.
The Judge secretly determines how long the hasty repairs last.
Gain +1 on attack throws against humans, elves, dwarves, halflings, gnomes, and Nobiran.
At level 7, the bonus increases to +2.
At level 13, the bonus increases to +3.
Gain +1 to throws to design, repair, and build automatons.
Can recognize most common automatons after careful investigation with a proficiency throw of 11+.
Cannot recognize uncommon or unique automatons.
Cannot discern command words.
Cannot assess the specific abilities of an item.
This proficiency can be selected multiple times.
Each additional selection adds another +1 bonus to design, repair, and build throws.
Each additional selection reduces the throw required to recognize common automatons by 4.
The machinist is focused on one customized personal automaton.
When first taken, the character immediately gains a personal automaton of the character's own design worth up to 7,000gp.
If the personal automaton is destroyed or disassembled, the character may design and/or build a new one.
The character may never have more than one personal automaton at a time.
Designing a personal automaton costs 7,000gp less than normal, with equivalent reductions in design time and library requirements.
A personal-automaton design can only be used by the character and only to build a personal automaton.
Building a personal automaton costs 7,000gp less than normal, with equivalent reductions in building time and workshop requirements.
A personal automaton requires daily maintenance from its builder of at least 1 turn per day.
If daily maintenance is not performed, the automaton is nonfunctional until 3d6 turns are spent returning it to working order.
Any proficiency throws to design and build personal automatons are always successful.
The character may disassemble the personal automaton for materials worth up to 50% of the unadjusted build cost.
Disassembly takes 1 day per 1,000gp of returned value.
Recovered materials may only offset the cost of constructing another personal automaton.
Personal automatons may be sold only for scrap value equal to 1/100 of build cost.
A personal automaton may not be controlled or operated by anyone other than the character.
The character can salvage spare parts and components from dwarven ruins, wrecked machines, and remnants of old automatons.
Reduces the cost to build or design automatons by 10%.
This proficiency can be selected multiple times.
Each additional selection reduces the cost to build or design automatons by an additional 10% of base cost.
The character may build automatons as if two class levels higher than actual level.
Time required to build an automaton is reduced by 20%.
When brawling, the character may deal lethal damage.
The character can punch or kick characters in metal armor without taking damage.
With a proficiency throw of 11+, the character can identify the abilities and vulnerabilities of various vermin from physical appearance.
The character receives a +1 bonus when making saving throws against special attacks by vermin.
